title: Platform-Specific Strategies
tagline: Year 4 — Adapting your plan to timer type, navigation rules, review flags and calculator access

introduction.overview: A strategy that works on a test with free navigation and an overall timer fails on a test with sectional timers and no return. Platform-specific strategy means choosing your plan after reading the rules: free navigation permits a two-pass plan; no return forces a plan that treats every question as final; a sectional timer needs a separate budget for each section; a calculator changes which questions are quick. This chapter works through these combinations with hypothetical rules; All figures and rules in this chapter's examples are hypothetical teaching examples and are not the rules of any real company or platform; always read the official instructions.
introduction.placementRelevance: Matching strategy to rules is the difference between a prepared and an unprepared candidate.
introduction.realWorldContext: Choosing a method to fit the constraints of a task is a general skill.

learningObjectives: Choose a plan for each timer and navigation combination

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Rules decide strategy: free navigation = two passes; no return = decide now; sectional = budget per section.

coreDefinitions: Free navigation: you may move back and forth.
No return: once you submit or move on, you cannot go back.
Sectional timer: a clock per section.
Final answer: an answer you cannot revise.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The same questions ask for different tactics under different rules.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: List the rules, then pick: pass structure, skip rule, review budget.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Skip rule
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Twice the pace (free) vs one pace (no return)

mainNarrative: With an overall timer and free navigation, do the quick questions first and return to the hard ones; the skip threshold is about twice your average pace.

With no return, skipping a question loses it permanently. The right rule is: attempt every question using elimination, spend more than the average only on questions with a good chance, and never leave a question blank if there is no penalty.
With sectional timers, a section left early gains nothing; use the full section time before moving on.
With an on-screen calculator, long divisions are quick; without it, prefer questions with simple numbers.
In each case read the rule in the official instructions, not in a forum.

deepDiveAspects.title: No return with penalty
deepDiveAspects.content: If skipping is allowed but returning is not, the decision to attempt is made once, using break-even chance.

deepDiveAspects.title: Time at the end of a section
deepDiveAspects.content: With sectional timers, leftover minutes are best spent re-checking flagged answers within the section.
